title: Arni Fricassee
subtitle: Greek lamb braised with lettuce and egg-lemon sauce
excerpt: Tender lamb shoulder cooked with lettuce and spring onions, finished with a sharp egg and lemon sauce. A classic Greek spring dish that is more satisfying than it looks.
sourceNotes: Classic Greek fricassee using avgolemono sauce; lettuce cooked in the braise is traditional and should not be replaced with another green.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Braise the lamb a day ahead and reheat gently. Add the lettuce and avgolemono sauce only just before serving.

content.text: Arni fricassee is a slow-braised lamb dish finished with avgolemono, a Greek egg and lemon sauce. The sauce is added off the heat and must not boil or it will curdle. Work quickly once you take the pot off the hob.
Season the lamb with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in the dutch oven over a high heat and brown the lamb in batches, about 3 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the spring onions to the pot and cook for 3 minutes until slightly softened. Return the lamb.
Pour in the stock. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 1 hour until the lamb is tender.
Add the lettuce and half the dill. Stir and cook uncovered for 5 minutes until the lettuce has wilted. Take the pot off the heat.
Whisk the egg yolks and lemon juice together in a bowl until combined. Ladle a spoonful of the hot broth into the egg mix while whisking constantly. Add two more ladlefuls the same way.
Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the pot. Stir gently. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon. Do not return to the heat.
Scatter the remaining dill over the top and rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve with crusty bread.

items.symptom: The egg sauce has curdled into lumps.
items.cause: The broth was too hot when added to the eggs, or the pot went back on the heat after the sauce was added.
items.fix: The dish is still edible but the texture is lost. Next time, take the pot fully off the heat and add the hot broth one ladle at a time, whisking steadily.

items.symptom: The lamb is tough after 1 hour.
items.cause: The heat was too low or the pieces were too large.
items.fix: Continue simmering for another 20 to 30 minutes with the lid on. Test with a fork; it should break apart without resistance.

items.cause: There was too much stock remaining, or the yolk ratio was low.
items.fix: Simmer the broth uncovered for 10 minutes before adding the lettuce to reduce it. A more concentrated broth gives a thicker sauce.
